Positive real numbers \( x, y, \) and \( z \) satisfy the following equations:

\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Compute the minimum possible value for \( x \).

Give the minimum value of x as an exact expression using only integers, rational numbers, and radicals (no trigonometric or inverse trigonometric functions, and no approximations).

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let

\[
p=\frac yx,\qquad q=\frac zy,\qquad r=\frac{xz}.
\]

Then \(p,q,r>0\) and \(pqr=1\). The given equations become

\[
3(1+p)(1+q)(1+r)=40
\]
and
\[
3(1-p)(1-q)(1-r)=4,
\]

so

\[
(1+p)(1+q)(1+r)=\frac{40}{3},\qquad
(1-p)(1-q)(1-r)=\frac43.
\]

Set

\[
A=1+p,\qquad B=1+q,\qquad C=1+r.
\]

Then

\[
ABC=\frac{40}{3},
\]
\[
(A-1)(B-1)(C-1)=1,
\]
\[
(2-A)(2-B)(2-C)=\frac43.
\]

Let \(S_1=A+B+C\), \(S_2=AB+BC+CA\), \(S_3=ABC\). Since \(S_3=\frac{40}{3}\),

\[
S_3-S_2+S_1=2
\]

and

\[
8-4S_1+2S_2-S_3=\frac43.
\]

Solving gives

\[
S_1=8,\qquad S_2=\frac{58}{3}.
\]

Thus \(A,B,C\) are the roots of

\[
T^3-8T^2+\frac{58}{3}T-\frac{40}{3}=0,
\]

or

\[
3T^3-24T^2+58T-40=0.
\]

This factors as

\[
(T-4)(3T^2-12T+10)=0,
\]

so

\[
\{A,B,C\}=\left\{4,\;2+\frac{\sqrt6}{3},\;2-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}\right\}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\{p,q,r\}
=
\left\{3,\;1+\frac{\sqrt6}{3},\;1-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}\right\}.
\]

Now \(y=px\) and \(z=pqx\), so from \(xyz=3\),

\[
x^3=\frac{3}{p^2q}.
\]

Because \(pqr=1\), we have \(p^2q=\frac pr\). To minimize \(x\), we maximize \(\frac pr\). The largest possible ratio is obtained by taking

\[
p=3,\qquad r=1-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Hence

\[
p^2q=\frac{3}{1-\frac{\sqrt6}{3}}=9+3\sqrt6,
\]

and so

\[
x_{\min}^3=\frac{3}{9+3\sqrt6}
=\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

Thus the minimum possible value of \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}}.
\]
